Downstream started. Comparing def37ce3 (target branch) with 4e023bc0 (this merge request). Run started by @AlphaTechini. Journeys first, then results.

## Journeys added

### Existing parts the change reaches (compared old against new)

**A reader signs up, adds books, lists and opens them, and hits bad input and missing books**
1. Sign up and log in.
2. Create a book with tags, then create the same book again.
3. Try to create a book with no token, with an empty title, and with too many tags.
4. List all books, list by a tag, and list by a tag nobody uses.
5. Open the new book, then open a book that does not exist.

Why it is in the run: calls the changed code. The list, open and create routes share the tag check and the Book type with the new similar-books code. Data accumulates over the iterations of a pass, so the list can pass its page size. Expected statuses come from handlers.go and auth.go.

**A reader puts a book on a shelf, lists the shelf, and a second reader checks their own shelf**
1. Sign up, log in and create a book.
2. Add the book to the shelf, then add it again.
3. Try to add a book with a negative id.
4. List the shelf with no token, then with the token.
5. A second reader signs up, logs in and lists their own shelf.

Why it is in the run: calls the changed code. The shelf routes share the tag check and the Book type with the new code. Expected statuses come from handlers.go and auth.go.

### New feature (new build only)

**A reader adds books with shared and unshared tags, then asks for similar books, including missing and odd ids**
1. Sign up and log in.
2. Create two books that share a tag and one book with no tags.
3. Ask for books similar to the first book, then ask again.
4. Ask for books similar to the second book and to the untagged book.
5. Ask for similar books for a book that does not exist and for a negative id.

Why it is in the run: new route. Expected statuses come from handlers.go.

### Controls

**A reader reviews a book and reads the reviews, with a bad rating and a missing book**
1. Check the health page, sign up and log in.
2. Create a book and review it.
3. Try a review with a rating outside the allowed range and a review for a missing book.
4. Read the reviews.

Why it is in the run: control. The review routes are outside the change, so this shows whether unrelated pages slow down while the new feature is in use.

Validation gave no warnings. The similar route is new, so no existing journey can reach it. Its not-found cases are covered in the new-feature journey.

**Not measured**

**Method.** Baseline run twice (B1, B2) and candidate once (C), in the order B1, C, B2, sequentially on one machine. Three runs give no confidence interval; treat verdicts near the thresholds as uncertain.

Gated metrics decide the verdict. For each, the worse baseline is the larger of B1 and B2, the noise band is the difference between them, and the allowed rise is the larger of a fraction of the worse baseline and an absolute figure. A metric is a regression when the candidate is above the worse baseline by more than the allowed rise and by more than the noise band, and improved by the opposite rule against the better baseline. When neither holds and the noise band is larger than the allowed rise, no verdict is given (withheld): a change of the allowed size could not be seen in this run. Smallest detectable is the larger of the allowed rise and the noise band. A step that passed on both baseline runs and failed on the candidate is a regression. One gated app metric clearly better and another clearly worse is reported as a trade-off.

Allowed rise by metric: CPU per completed journey 20% of the worse baseline; Bytes written per journey the larger of 1% of the worse baseline and an absolute 1024; Write syscalls per journey 4% of the worse baseline; Open fds an absolute 1; Threads an absolute 2; Peak RSS 5% of the worse baseline; Heap objects allocated per journey the larger of 10% of the worse baseline and an absolute 100; Heap bytes allocated per journey the larger of 5% of the worse baseline and an absolute 16384; GC cycles per pass an absolute 2; Goroutines an absolute 1.

Latency is advisory: a latency or total CPU figure is called slower when the candidate is worse than the worse baseline run by more than 2 times the noise band (the difference between B1 and B2), by at least 20%, and by at least 10 ms (latency) or 0.5 s (CPU). It never opens an issue.

Issues opened by this run:

- #18 "[Downstream] app: CPU per journey up 22.54 ms/journey (+684%)". It covers CPU per journey and peak memory, which are the two gated regressions in the report. The report has no trade-off questions.

Two problems with #18 need a human:

1. The issue tool returned `description: null` when I read the issue back. The body may not have been saved. If the description is empty, "fix it" and "verify" on #18 cannot work, because they read the "Downstream state" marker from the description. The exact engine text is in `/tmp/ds/issues.json` on the runner. Re-run Downstream on this merge request to regenerate it.
2. When I copied the body, I mistyped the "Smallest detectable" column for two rows of the last journey table. The `log_in` row shows 232.0% and the `sign_up` row shows 232.0%. The engine's figures are 144.7% for `log_in` and 232.0% for `sign_up`, and the report note above has them correctly. Please trust the report note, not #18, for those two cells.

Downstream does not merge or approve. This merge request is a draft marked "Do not merge".

Why: new route. Matching books pile up over the passes of the run.

**Method.** Baseline run twice (B1, B2) and candidate once (C), in the order B1, C, B2, sequentially on one machine. Three runs give no confidence interval; treat verdicts near the thresholds as uncertain.

Gated metrics decide the verdict. For each, the worse baseline is the larger of B1 and B2, the noise band is the difference between them, and the allowed rise is the larger of a fraction of the worse baseline and an absolute figure. A metric is a regression when the candidate is above the worse baseline by more than the allowed rise and by more than the noise band, and improved by the opposite rule against the better baseline. When neither holds and the noise band is larger than the allowed rise, no verdict is given (withheld): a change of the allowed size could not be seen in this run. Smallest detectable is the larger of the allowed rise and the noise band. A step that passed on both baseline runs and failed on the candidate is a regression. One gated app metric clearly better and another clearly worse is reported as a trade-off.

Allowed rise by metric: CPU per completed journey 20% of the worse baseline; Bytes written per journey the larger of 1% of the worse baseline and an absolute 1024; Write syscalls per journey 4% of the worse baseline; Open fds an absolute 1; Threads an absolute 2; Peak RSS the larger of 5% of the worse baseline and an absolute 10; Heap objects allocated per journey the larger of 10% of the worse baseline and an absolute 100; Heap bytes allocated per journey the larger of 5% of the worse baseline and an absolute 16384; GC cycles per pass an absolute 2; Goroutines an absolute 1.

Latency is advisory: a latency or total CPU figure is called slower when the candidate is worse than the worse baseline run by more than 2 times the noise band (the difference between them), by at least 20%, and by at least 10 ms (latency) or 0.5 s (CPU). It never opens an issue.
